face_detection.name: RetinaFace (det_10g)
face_detection.notes: Downloaded automatically by insightface on first run. The doubled 'models/' is real, not a typo: FaceAnalysis(root=MODEL_DIR) appends its own 'models' directory, so with MODEL_DIR=./models the bundle lands at ./models/models/buffalo_l/. FaceEmbedder drops every model in the bundle except detection + recognition at load.

face_recognition.notes: Downloaded automatically by insightface on first run. Same doubled-'models/' path as face_detection.

bib_detection.name: YOLOv8n Bib Detector
bib_detection.notes: Trained and deployed (2026-03-21) on 1,713 Roboflow-annotated event photos. Exported with a STATIC input shape, so the decode dimension never reaches the detector — Ultralytics letterboxes every input down to 640 before the ONNX session and rescales boxes back. MAX_INFERENCE_DIMENSION therefore only affects the crop resolution handed to PaddleOCR, not detection. A dynamic re-export would also need simplify=False (the simplifier folds the dynamic axis back to static — see export_blur_classifier.py) AND an imgsz argument in BibDetector, which currently passes none; measured benefit is unproven (1024 vs 1280 gave identical detections). Source checkpoint: runs/detect/detect/bib_det/weights/best.pt.

bib_ocr.name: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5
bib_ocr.notes: Not stored under models/. PaddleOCR downloads and caches its own weights outside this directory (~/.paddleocr or PADDLE_PDX_MODEL_SOURCE), so there is no artifact here to point at. file is null rather than a path that never resolves.

blur_classifier.name: YOLOv8n-cls Blur Classifier (4-class)
blur_classifier.notes: Historical top-1 98.68% was measured on a random file split where 99% of validation images share a shoot with training; it is not field accuracy. On 856 sharp real marathon frames from three events this artifact flagged 61% as blurry (vault journal 2026-09-29-blur-detection-investigation-and-improvement-plan). Re-exported 2026-08-14 with dynamic=True: the batch axis is dynamic so classify_batch issues one (N,3,224,224) ONNX call instead of a per-image loop. Ultralytics also makes H/W dynamic; the wrapper always centre-crops and resizes to 224 so that is inert. Verified bit-identical to the previous static export (max abs diff 0.0) and batched-vs-per-image agreement within float32 epsilon. Measured CPU gain is small (~1.06x on 50 images) because the model is tiny and ONNX Runtime already parallelises a single inference — batching is what pays off on GPU. Required in the blur profile; optional in the full profile. Re-run export_blur_classifier.py to regenerate with a new artifact version and digests; it self-verifies the dynamic axis.

person_detector.name: YOLOv8n-seg COCO person detector (stage 2 of the blur classifier)
person_detector.notes: Only the person class (index 0) is read; each person's mask gives its own pixels for the sharpness measure. Letterbox, score filter, NMS and mask decoding live in src/ml/blur/person_detector.py, so serving needs no torch or Ultralytics. Licence AGPL-3.0 (owner decision 2026-10-06).
